# Examination outline templates

Placeholders are illustrative. Fill them only from the record.

## Header

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Witness | Name and role |
| Forum and stage | Trial, hearing, deposition, or investigation interview |
| Form | Direct, cross, deposition, or hearing |
| Objective (one sentence) | What the examination must establish or undo |
| Elements or issues served | Each with its source |
| Prior statements and documents | Each with source ID and pinpoint |
| Time allowed or limits | From the court's order or rule, or UNVERIFIED |

## Question table (all forms)

| No. | Topic | Question | Style | Expected answer | Source and pinpoint | Exhibit | Purpose | Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Style is open, leading, or locking. Direct uses open questions; cross uses leading, one-fact questions.

## Direct

1. Background and role, kept short.
2. Each topic in the order that makes the account clear.
3. Foundation for each exhibit before the exhibit is offered.
4. Closing question that returns to the objective.

## Cross

1. Chapters that each end on one useful admission.
2. One fact per question; no "why" questions unless the answer is known and safe.
3. Stop after the admission; do not ask the witness to explain it.

## Deposition

| Step | Purpose | Example question type |
|---|---|---|
| Locking | Fix the account before it can shift | "Is that everything you remember about X?" |
| Source of knowledge | Separate what the witness saw from what the witness was told | "How do you know that?" |
| Documents | Identify, authenticate, and date each document | "Is this the report you wrote?" |
| Follow-up | Close gaps the answers opened | Targeted, one fact each |

## Impeachment sequence (one per contradiction)

| Step | Content |
|---|---|
| Commit | Get the witness to affirm today's testimony. Source: today's testimony, page and line. |
| Credit | Establish that the earlier statement was made, when, to whom, and in what setting. Source for each fact. |
| Confront | Read the earlier words exactly, then ask whether they were said. Quote, source, pinpoint. |
| Control | Close on the single admission the contradiction yields and stop; do not ask the witness to explain it. |
| Verify before use (not a courtroom step) | Confirm that the quote matches the original file character for character. Initials and date. |

## Exhibit and foundation table

| Exhibit | What it is | Foundation questions | Admissibility basis (rule and source, or "unresolved") | Offered through |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Objection and response table

| Likely objection | When it arises | Response | Authority (verified with date, or UNVERIFIED) |
|---|---|---|---|

## Rehabilitation

List the points the other side may use to restore the witness and the answer to each.

## Must-get admissions

| Admission | Source showing the witness can give it | If the witness refuses |
|---|---|---|

## Do-not-ask list

Questions whose answers are unknown or harmful, with the reason each is excluded.
